questions.def: Use comparative adjectives (ending in -er) for short adjectives.
questions.question: The weather is ___ than it was yesterday.

questions.def: Use adverbs to modify verbs (spoke).
questions.question: She spoke ___ about her experiences.

questions.def: 'Felt' is a linking verb; use an adjective (bad), not an adverb.
questions.question: He felt badly about missing the deadline again.

questions.def: 'Was' requires an adjective (clear) to describe the subject.
questions.question: It was ___ that he was upset.

questions.def: Use superlative adjectives (worst) with 'ever seen'.
questions.question: This is the ___ movie I have ever seen.

questions.def: Use 'much' to modify comparatives (better).
questions.question: He did ___ better than I expected.

questions.def: Do not use 'more' with '-er' comparatives. 'Faster' is correct.
questions.question: She drives more faster than I do now.

questions.def: Need an adverb (patiently) to modify the verb 'waited'.
questions.question: She waited ___ for her turn.

questions.def: Need an adjective (careless) to describe the noun 'driver'.
questions.question: He is a ___ driver, but he is learning.

questions.def: Use 'the more...the better' structure for parallel increase.
questions.question: The ___ I study, the better I understand.

questions.def: Need an adverb (skillfully) to modify the verb 'performed'.
questions.question: She performed ___ at the concert.

questions.def: 'Late' means not on time. 'Lately' means recently.
questions.question: They arrived ___ for the meeting.

questions.def: 'Slightly' modifies comparative adjectives.
questions.question: She is ___ taller than her sister.

questions.def: Adjectives come before 'enough' (old enough).
questions.question: He is enough old to vote in this election.

questions.def: Need an adverb (certainly) to modify the verb 'spoke'.
questions.question: He spoke ___ about his future plans.

questions.def: 'Tasted' is a linking verb; use an adjective (delicious).
questions.question: The food tasted ___.

questions.def: Use the base adjective form after 'as'.
questions.question: He is not as ___ as he seems.

questions.def: Need an adverb (attentively) to modify the verb 'listened'.
questions.question: She listened ___ to the speaker.

questions.def: 'Incredibly' is an adverb modifying the adjective 'good'.
questions.question: She is ___ good at playing the piano.

questions.def: Use an adverb (irresponsibly) to modify the verb 'behaved'.
questions.question: He behaved ___.

questions.def: Need an adverb (fluently) to modify the verb 'speaks'.
questions.question: She speaks English ___.

questions.def: Need an adverb (beautifully) to modify the verb 'painted'.
questions.question: He painted the wall ___.

questions.def: 'Highly' modifies the adjective 'talented'.
questions.question: She is a ___ talented musician.

questions.def: 'Felt' is a linking verb; use an adjective (sad), not an adverb.
questions.question: He felt sadly when he heard the news.

questions.def: Need an adverb (quickly) to modify the verb 'responded'.
questions.question: He responded ___ to the email.

questions.def: 'Perfectly' is an adverb modifying the adjective 'clear'.
questions.question: The instructions were ___ clear.

questions.def: 'Too' is used to indicate excessiveness.
questions.question: She is ___ busy to talk right now.

questions.def: "Considerably" is an adverb modifying the adjective "longer."
questions.question: The report was ___ longer than expected.

questions.def: "Candidly" is the correct adverb to modify "spoke."
questions.question: She spoke ___ about her experiences.

questions.def: The correct structure is 'the more, the more'.
questions.question: The harder you practise, more skilled you become.
